main_issue: Whether alcohol is served at the shared housewarming given Agent D's religious discomfort as a host, versus A's purchase and B's invited colleagues expecting drinks.

A-B.evidence: A cites B's invited colleagues (T10) and asks if B wants to send guests to a bar (T12); B refuses the bar idea (T13), both keeping alcohol at the party.

A-C.evidence: C proposes both drinks and soft drinks (T6) and a balcony cooler (T16), which keeps A's drinks in use; A never replies, but A's stance is compatible.

A-D.evidence: A says 'I've already bought all this... what do you want us to do?' (T10) and rejects D's alcohol-free plan (T12); D has not accepted the cooler by T16.

B-C.evidence: C's balcony cooler explicitly serves 'your colleagues can still get a drink' (T16), matching B's need; B's reply is not given.

B-D.evidence: B says it's a problem (T5) and 'I can't do that' to D's bar proposal (T13); D remains uncomfortable.

C-D.evidence: D rejects 'other options' (T7, T9); later D says 'You're right. We need to figure this out' (T15), and C offers the cooler as a compromise (T16) with no response yet.
